mentions.name: ministar
mentions.description: Astrophotography tool that automates the hard parts of untracked astrophotography: it uses plate solving to help point the camera at the target and live-stacks captures while accounting for the rotation of the Earth. It is early-stage and hacky, with plans to port to Linux/Raspberry Pi so a minimal high-quality astronomy setup (DSLR, 3-way head, tripod, power bank, and a single-board computer) can be used anywhere. Early results include shots of the h-Persei cluster.
mentions.source_excerpt: The second thing I'm working on is an astrophotography tool called ministar (https://github.com/galbacarys/ministar). The premise is basically, let's automate the hard parts of untracked astrophotography by using plate solving to help you point your camera to your target, and then live-stacking the result taking into account the rotation of the Earth.
